subject: Emotions
title: Self-Disgust
description: A short lesson to help you apply Self-Disgust.

hook.text: After a moral failure, people describe wanting to 'scrub themselves clean.' The metaphor is physical.

buildup.text: Self-disgust turns the rejection reflex inward. You become the contamination you want to avoid.

discovery.text: The 'Macbeth effect'—people who recall shameful acts wash their hands longer. Guilt feels physically dirty.

twist.text: Self-disgust correlates with depression more strongly than guilt or shame alone.

climax.text: Therapy for self-disgust works by breaking the link between 'I did bad' and 'I am contaminated.'

punchline.text: The hardest disgust to clean is aimed at yourself.
